doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: How he came to attend Hamilton
summary: Sent from Sweden to his uncle in Larchmont, he went to high school there, toured colleges with the Sanborns, and chose Hamilton over Colgate.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Ah. Luck. Two things have been lucky in my life. I had graduated from high school in Sweden and I had no idea what I wanted to do. And my father said, “We’ll send you to America.” He had a younger brother in Larchmont, New York, and I came, by myself on the boat, ten days on the ship, and arrived her as a 17-year-old. So what my father basically did was he foisted the indecision of a teenager onto his younger brother. And luckily, well I came in August and of course high school, I had a cousin who was a senior in Mamaroneck High School, and when he went off to school I was sitting around the house and waiting for him to finish school and come home and then we could go out and join with his friends and stuff. And my uncle said, “We can’t have a young fellow like you sitting around the house here, I’m going to write to your father, I’m going to become your guardian and you can go to the high school on my taxes. So that’s what happened. I came to the high school maybe three or four weeks late, and I was good at ice hockey. I was on the ice hockey team in the winter at Hamilton. And one of the fathers of one of my teammates said to my uncle, “I’m going to take my son to see some colleges, do you mind if I take your nephew?” I had no idea about higher education in America. So I went with Jack Sanborn and Mr. Sanborn and we drove up and we saw Colgate and we saw Hamilton. I stayed at the Deke House because Jerry Steiner was older and he was from

Larchmont and he was the goalie on the hockey team. I stayed at the fraternity house, the Deke fraternity house, while Mr. Sanborn and Jack, his son, went off to see Williams. Because I said I’ve seen enough. I’ve seen two colleges. I don’t need to go. They came back and got me. And then Jack and I — then we both applied to Hamilton. And actually we filled out our applications at Mr. Sandborn’s house in Larchmont. And he helped that. And I came up for an interview, and both Jack and I were accepted and we decided to come here and we roomed together first year.
Do you remember what the tuition was?
It’s gone up a little bit.

I understand. Well I mean it was a smaller college, there were only men, and that’s one reason why I picked it over Colgate because I thought, first of all I thought it might be a little academically better and I felt that that would be good, but it was smaller. I thought you wouldn’t get lost.
